items.text: Hello Wanderers,
We’ve listened to your feedback and what you want for the future, and we’re working on
it. As a way to kick off our Q4 2026 roadmap, we’re starting with the ‘Lost & Found’
update, a cosmetic pack to ensure that you enter the upcoming updates in style.
Our new ‘Lost & Found’ update brings 2 FREE wanderer skins and 5 DLC skins in the
‘Lost & Found Cosmetic Pack’. The update will go live October 29th and is the first step
in our roadmap for the rest of the year! We also plan to release new levels – more
information will be coming soon about this one.
We appreciate your patience while we wrangle entities and discover new liminal spaces
to explore.

items.text: Wanderers, for the first time since 1.0's October launch, another abandoned M.E.G facility has been located, leading into a children's hospital conjoined with... Bruce’s Ball Pit?
Push through the endless polymer of Level 421 and escape into Overgrowth when the Plastic Mariana level no-clips onto all platforms on August 27th.

Some of you keen-eared folks may have noticed a new rendition of Ins0mics iconic main backrooms motif. We’ve worked together with the incredible Norwegian Producer and DJ, Vairo, to create a terrifying song aptly named “Wanderer.” A big thank you to Vairo for producing this song for us, and to Ins0mic for allowing us to recreate and use the motif.
You can find the full Wanderer song on Vairo’s Spotify and YouTube.

Today we are releasing a new bugfix patch, ironing out some more mischief the entities have caused since the update on May 28th, which included the console launch and cross-platform matchmaking.

Thank you so much for all of your reports and the amount of information provided – it has been pivotal for us to help get these fixed! If you experience any further bugs, or want to provide feedback and suggestions, please make a ticket on our Feature Upvote page. We are still investigating some commonly reported issues, such as FPS causing some sensitivity issues.

items.text: Hey Wanderers!

Today we are releasing our first bug fix patch for Escape the Backrooms since the May 28 PC update and launch on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5. In-game, this update will appear as version 1.3.1 (3597) on all platforms. The patch addresses a number of player reports since the May 28 update and introduces more improvements.

We are working hard on addressing as many reports as possible, including multiplayer connection and voice chat bugs that you’ve been reporting (thanks so much for that!) We have some fixes in this patch, and more are planned in future updates, as the team continues to investigate and prioritise these topics. In case you missed it, we have a quick form for these two points we’d love for you to fill in, so we can get as much information as possible over to the crew.

releases.displayName: Console Launch and Steam Patch NOW LIVE! Full Details Here

items.text: Hey Wanderers. Surprise!

Today is the day. A new host of friends have found their way no-clipping into the Backrooms, as Escape the Backrooms is now available on Xbox Series X|S – including PC and Xbox Game Pass - and PlayStation 5.

Team up with these new folks using the brand-new cross-platform lobby code system, create new friends and memories, and most importantly, dance around the party table in Level Fun while humming You Day and chugging Almond Water! Oh, and not dying I suppose...
As part of this update, we have released a patch right here on Steam, adding the new matchamking system alongside more fixes and improvements. Here are the patch notes below:
Added cross-platform matchmaking via Epic Online Services (EOS) without the need to sign into an Epic account.
Added new lobby codes to allow players to join lobbies for both private and public lobbies.
Option added to hide the lobby code, to avoid unwanted party members joining.
Cross-platform matchmaking can be disabled in the settings.
Cross-platform players will have a logo beside their username to indicate their platform.
A warning is displayed alerting players if cross-platform matchmaking is enabled
Voice chat is functional on all platforms.
You can now select a player to mute voice chat, text chat (PC only), kick, block, or report them.
Player scoreboard has now moved into the settings.
Players can be muted, kicked, blocked, or reported in the settings.
Added the ability to block and report players in case of spamming/griefing, etc.
A blocked player list is accessible within the main menu or lobby, allowing players to be removed from the list at any time.
An auto save icon message will display at the start of the game, alerting players to the icon.
The auto save will appear between level transitions or certain respawn points in a level, alerting a player to where they can resume from.
Profanity filters now occur in text chat and player names.
Due to a bug in its functionality, the HDR setting has been removed. We are investigating a fix and will re-enable this functionality when the issue has been resolved.
Updated translations for level names and descriptions in Traditional Chinese, Polish, and Brazilian Portuguese.
Updated EULA.
Fixed an issue that prevented players progressing in the second part of the “Cave System” level on low graphics settings due to missing shadows.
The ‘Apply' or ‘Keep Old’ settings option after making a settings change now functions as expected.
The ’Show Game Chat’ setting can now be selected when navigating up or down with the D-pad.
A button has been added for a controller user to use the 'Restore Defaults' option.
The resolution will now reset to the default resolution when using the ‘Restore Defaults’ button.
An error message will now occur if the host of a lobby disconnects from the internet.
Clients that are kicked can no longer rejoin a lobby.
The correct messaging will now be displayed when the game host leaves a session.
Improved readability on the screens in Hub Area when graphic settings are set to low.
Fixed an issue preventing clients from leaving a lobby if the Ready button wasn’t highlighted when using a controller.
Audio settings are correctly applied after changing them, no longer requiring the game to be restarted.
The initial visual state of some settings is correctly reverted after closing the settings menu without applying the settings.
The ‘Show Body' setting can now be re-enabled if previously disabled.
Players are now informed that the lobby is full when they fail to join.
The ‘Apply' button now correctly appears when editing settings in the Controls or Game tab in the settings menu.
Fixed an issue in Russian where the added XP value was shown incorrectly.
Voice chat is now correctly off in both lobby and in-game if turned off in the settings.
Fixed an issue preventing the correct code from triggering the Security Terminal.
Fixed a rare issue where the ‘quit game' module loses focus with joysticks.
Fixed an issue where The Hub displayed difficulty information rather than a level description for the host when initially creating a lobby.
The ’Enter Save Game Name’ option can no longer be interacted with while the ‘Return to Main Menu?’ pop-up is active.
The ‘Show Event Content’ option is not automatically set to ‘Enabled’ upon restarting the game.
Phew, that was a lot. Now, don’t mind us, we’re just gonna switch gears for a bit...

releases.displayName: New Free Outfits and More Fixes: Chinese New Year Update Drops February 12

items.text: Hello Wanderers!

The next free update for Escape the Backrooms drops on February 12 – the Chinese New Year update! This will include six new cosmetic costumes to choose from, alongside further improvements and fixes across the game.

With the Year of the Horse beginning on February 17 this year, some costumes and patterns in the update are inspired by this animal, along with other traditions of the Spring Festival celebration –combined of course with an Escape the Backrooms twist…

The ‘Year of the Horse’ outfit brings the traditional brocade shirt and material alongside some dashing horse ears, whilst the ‘Golden Threads’ option features a horse artwork with Sakura blossoms. ‘Jockey Wanderer’ is a nod to the popular horse racing event around the Chinese New Year and includes a ‘922’ patch in reference to an elusive Backrooms level. ‘Lion Dance Wanderer’ takes the iconic designs from this street celebration to make a fun outfit including a full head cover. ‘Brocade Wanderer’ reflects traditional Chinese garments, and ‘Lantern Wanderer’ uses a pattern showing the lights that symbolise new beginnings and good fortune. Perhaps it’ll help keep those Skin Stealers at bay...

The six costumes are free and available to all players, available in the usual spot to switch up your Wanderer’s look, first added in December’s Winter Wanderer update. Alongside these additions, the update will also have more fixes and improvements driven by community feedback. We’ll share up the patch notes on February 12.

Looking further forward, the crew are busy at work with plans to continue expanding Escape the Backrooms. This includes brand new levels, which are currently in their design phase! We’re also working hard on the required tweaks to launch Escape the Backrooms on consoles, and will share more information on this as soon as it’s locked in.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42189581/d5d7a67263e9fde7b92cbb586452abe316838877.png"]

releases.displayName: Winter Wanderer – Free Festive Update Out Now!

items.text: 🎶 Walking in a winter wander(er)land… 🎶

Time to celebrate this wonderful time of the year in the best way possible – navigating unnerving spaces and avoiding a grizzly death by terrifying Entities. The free ‘Winter Wanderer’ update for Escape the Backrooms launches on Steam on December 10!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42189581/e4c0507d7c93856ef08acac7d6d8f08a21dd9bb5.jpg"]

This update and content drop, free to all players on Steam, adds a range of winter and festive-themed outfits to select for your Wanderer. From reindeer, to snowflakes, to an oil rig-based reference… there’s a little something for everyone’s taste in here.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42189581/c36057099f79dbd91bb9beb0915f41a3d15d8dbd.jpg"]

Adding the cosmetic options also means the addition of a ‘character select’ screen, so you can choose which outfit to don before diving into the Backrooms. We’re hyped to add this and will be adding more customisation options in future updates!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42189581/0715f7a8889b25ece9036c7274a27abba308d14e.jpg"]
Alongside the new content, Update 1.1 brings some more fixes and improvements based on community feedback. The full patch notes are available below.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42189581/55599ff71211e40c1aa07980388d2d694df5df72.jpg"]
PATCH NOTES FOR UPDATE 1.1 (WINTER WANDERER UPDATE)
Added screens and functionality to select different player outfits, available from the main menu
Added 11 new player outfits to select – eight festive themed outfits, along with red, blue, and green versions of the default Wanderer outfit
Nightmare Mode – checkpoints and save files are no longer accessible and the mode works as intended. If any player dies at any point in the playthrough, all players must restart from the beginning
Fixed instances of players being able to see through walls after adjusting visual settings
Level 0 – Fixed rare instances of the Bacteria entity falling out of the map
Level 4 – corrected the behaviour of camera detection
Added functionality and on-screen messaging to inform players if they are matched with a player on a different version of the game, which can happen if a players does not update their game
Fixed rare instances of items not appearing correctly when held by a player, with specific visual settings applied
Hello Wanderers!

The first patch for Escape the Backrooms Version 1.0 on Steam is rolling out now. This patch focuses on resolving as many community-reported topics as possible at this stage, and a few more pesky bugs identified by our team.
Below are the patch notes for any noticeable fixes or changes in the 1.01 update, releasing today on Steam:
1.01 Patch Notes
Functionality for PlayStation controller is now enabled on Steam
Fixed issue causing player to immediately drink Almond Water after picking the item up, when playing with a controller
Fixed instances of the spectator camera, after dying, locking to just one other player
Fixed issues causing performance drops when in Laundry room of Level 188
Fixed issue causing players to sometimes become stuck in the wall near the beginning of Level 922
Fixed issue allowing players to get stuck behind the auto-closing gate in Level 2
Fixed issue in Level 37 where if the player in control of steering the boat dies, the boat is no longer usable
Fixed visual error in levelling UI that can show the player receiving an infinite or extreme amount of XP
Fixed instances of the VHS/static on-screen effect unexpectedly moving and affecting click collision points
Fixed instances of keyboard bindings randomly changing to use gamepad controls on startup
Fixed error allowing the possibility of the Use Item option to be bound to multiple buttons
Fixed visual error when players first choose to ‘restore default controls’ in the Settings. Default settings will now appear correctly
Additions to the logos and updates to legal text on startup
Credits updated

As well as resolving this stuff for 1.01, the Escape the Backrooms team are looking into more player-reported topics as we speak, with an aim to bring fixes in future patches and updates. We’re looking into reports around Nightmare mode saves, sporadic reports of ‘Fatal Error’ crashes, entity behaviour in Level 37.2, and more.

To help players with sharing their feedback, and for our crew to track and take action on what you’re reporting, we’ve implemented a new system for reporting issues and feedback, via Feature Upvote. We encourage all players to share anything you’d like our team to investigate via this tool, and check out existing submissions in case you want to upvote them.
Take a look here
Thank you Wanderers – enjoy the 1.01 update!
Wanderers, we have an update for Escape the Backrooms rolling out today on Steam!

To be totally clear straight away: this is not the 1.0 release of the game. Escape the Backrooms is still in Early Access, and this is officially ‘Hotfix #23’, with all credit to Secret Mode for going back into the current version and adding patches for some of the bugs we already fixed for 1.0.

While we make the final tweaks required for the 1.0 launch, we didn’t want to hold back some fixes and improvements to the current game, so we’re rolling out this small update. It addresses more of the community’s recent feedback and reports, including:
• Garage: Middle Floor - Some hints will last longer on screen
• Garage: Level 2 - Fixed players being able to walk through a specific wall
• Hotel - Fixed moth jelly occasionally falling through the floor in the Hotel lobby
• Poolrooms - Stopped the Hydrolitis plague from insta-killing players, and death will now cause ragdolling

• Level Fun (Expanded) – Improved visuals and disabled flashlights in upper level of zone 3
• Tunnel – Some hints will last longer on screen, and disabled ability for Bacteria looking up
We hope you enjoy this small update, and will keep you in the loop as we complete the final work for the 1.0 launch of Escape the Backrooms!
